Steve.  Our reception team try to help our patients and guide them through our systems set by the NHS and the practice to ensure all our patients receive safe care.  They do not create the rules.  Often anger is aimed at them, and that is why we protect our staff with our zero tolerance anger policy. A zero tolerance policy towards violent, threatening and abusive behaviour is now in place throughout the National Health Service. The staff in this practice have the right to work in an environment free from violent, threatening or abusive behaviour and everything will be done to protect that right. At no time will any violent, threatening or abusive behaviour be tolerated towards staff, patients or other visitors to the practice. This relates to any form of abuse from patients or staff which includes (but is not limited to) sexism, racism homophobia, biphobia, transphobia and ageism, or harassment or abuse on basis of disability, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, religion or belief. 
Our Practice staff aim to be polite, helpful, and sensitive to all patients’ individual needs and circumstances. They would respectfully remind patients that very often staff could be confronted with a multitude of varying and sometimes difficult tasks and situations, all at the same time.  The staff understand that ill patients do not always act in a reasonable manner and will take this into consideration when trying to deal with a misunderstanding or complaint.
If you are still experiencing an issue please contact Diane, our Governance and Patient Experience Manager at the practice who will provide assistance. Many thanks Firstly, I am sorry to learn that you are unhappy with the care that you have received from the practice and the distress the situation has caused you.  I am grateful that you have brought this to our attention.  
As I understand it you are complaining because of a recent consultation with our ACP.
The practice takes all complaints seriously and your complaint has been investigated in line with our complaints procedure. This involved me speaking to our ACP, who provided me with an account of their recollections of what happened, as well as reviewing your medical records.  
From your records I can see you completed a triage form request for an appointment on Thursday 17th October at 3.28pm stating you had a chest infection for one week.  This form was triaged by the duty doctor, Dr Yelland, who actioned this request and he felt it was appropriate for you to see our Advanced Care Practitioner with an urgent appointment for your symptoms.  Our ACP’s are fully qualified clinicians and are more than capable of treating a chest infection without the need to see a doctor. 
At 3.39pm on the 17th a member of our reception team booked you an appointment for later that day, 17th October at 5pm. You arrived before your appointment time at 4.43pm, and was seen at 5.35pm.  This was a 35 minute delay.  The ACP apologises for this delay and explains this was due to her seeing a child earlier in her clinic who’s appointment over ran, and the subsequent appointments were running behind.  Unfortunately it is hard for us to predict medical emergencies and the length of time they will take, however, we do build blocks into the clinics to allow clinicians time to catch up and prevent delays to patients.  On this occasion the ACP was still running behind.
Reviewing her consultation she did full diagnostics for a chest infection, she enquired if you had tried anything prior to the appointment and you advised over the counter treatments.  She asked if you had tried things in the past that had worked for you and you advised antibiotics and inhalers.  She documented a treatment plan and a safety net then prescribed antibiotics.  This is in response to her findings and your responses.
With regards to your opinion of myself, I’m not aware that we have ever met, but I am happy to arrange a meeting to discuss your issues further with regards to the practice.  We welcome all feedback and encourage our patients to feedback and suggest improvements.  We also encourage you to join our Patient Participation Group that meets regularly.  This group often discusses challenges that patients face and help work with the practice staff to resolve and improve our services.  If this is something you would be interested in please contact our reception and ask for the Office Managers who run the PPG.
I am sorry for the distress that this situation has caused you.  We are appreciative of you bringing this to our attention and providing us with an opportunity to learn and make any necessary changes going forward.  
I hope that we have been able to fully address your concerns and questions.  Please do not hesitate to contact me at the surgery if you feel that you need to discuss this further.
If you’re not happy with our final response to your complaint and would like to take the matter further, you can contact the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman. The Ombudsman makes final decisions on complaints that have not been resolved by the NHS, government departments and some other public organisations. The service is free for everyone. To take a complaint to the Ombudsman, go to www.ombudsman.org.uk/making-complaint or call 0345 015 4033. It is important that you make the complaint as soon as you receive our final response as there are time limits for the Ombudsman to look into complaints’.

From your medical records i cannot see that you have requested an appointment recently.  The last time you attended surgery was the 9th May and you booked this on the 11th April. On 15th April we introduced a total triage system where patients can request an appointment by completing an online form.  A GP then triages this form and determines the most appropriate clinician and urgency for the appointment.  Since introducing this service most patients have received an appointment within 0-3 days if urgent, and up to 10 working days if deemed routine.  Patient choice can effect this, but overall we feel this change has massively changed our appointment system for the better for our patients.
we hope that we have been able to fully address your concerns and questions.  Please do not hesitate to contact me at the surgery if you feel that you need to discuss this further.

Alison, thank you for your feedback.  We are sorry you had a poor experience from the surgery. Total Triage is a new approach recommended by NHS England, to improve accessibility to Primary Care services. The main objectives are to enhance the quality of care our patients receive, to ensure that they are given the most appropriate appointment or advice to meet their needs and that this is done in a timely way. All patients will complete a short form, either via our website, or by the reception team who will complete this form on the patients behalf.  This is to ensure that our patients who are unable to access the internet or do not have a smart phone have the same accessibility.  
The form is triaged by the triage GP who will decide which member of our healthcare team is best placed to help, the most suitable time frame for the appointment and whether it is best suited to be via telephone or in person at the practice. 
The new system also aims to reduce the 8am rush on the telephones, as patients can bypass our reception team and access the forms themselves via our website and at their leisure.   Already, the practice has seen an increase in capacity with more appointments available to patients within a shorter time frame.  We have to put capacity limits into the system so that both patients and staff are safe, and once our safe limit has been reached for the day you may be told to try again the following day.  If it is an emergency you will be advised to attend A&E, as this is best placed for a medical emergency that cannot wait 24hours.
We hope to support patients and their families/carers to get used to the new way of contacting the practice and to become comfortable with this over time.  We will, of course, provide additional support to those patients who are unable to use online resources.  
We continue to advise that if you cannot use the internet for any reason, please call us – we will enter your details into our website for you. This may take longer than our previous system, so please be patient.  We apologise again and will take your feedback on We are sorry your mother had a poor experience from the surgery. Total Triage is a new approach recommended by NHS England, to improve accessibility to Primary Care services. The main objectives are to enhance the quality of care our patients receive, to ensure that they are given the most appropriate appointment or advice to meet their needs and that this is done in a timely way. All patients will complete a short form, either via our website, or by the reception team who will complete this form on the patients behalf.  This is to ensure that our patients who are unable to access the internet or do not have a smart phone have the same accessibility.  We are sorry that on this occasion this did not happen.
The form is triaged by the triage GP who will decide which member of our healthcare team is best placed to help, the most suitable time frame for the appointment and whether it is best suited to be via telephone or in person at the practice. 
The new system also aims to reduce the 8am rush on the telephones, as patients can bypass our reception team and access the forms themselves via our website and at their leisure.   Already, the practice has seen an increase in capacity with more appointments available to patients within a shorter time frame.  Unfortunately, when you called at 2pm we had reached our safe capacity for urgent requests and this is why you were directed to 111 or A&E, of if the request was routine you could complete a request the following day.  We have to put capacity limits into the system so that both patients and staff are safe.  
We hope to support patients and their families/carers to get used to the new way of contacting the practice and to become comfortable with this over time.  We will, of course, provide additional support to those patients who are unable to use online resources.  
We continue to advise that if you cannot use the internet for any reason, please call us – we will enter your details into our website for you. This may take longer than our previous system, so please be patient.  We apologise again and will take your feedback on board.",null,[0,238]]]],[null,null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/reviews/data=!4m8!14m7!1m6!2m5!1sChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNUel9fMkxREAE!2m1!1s0x0:0xcea845eb0329d060!3m1!1s2@1:CIHM0ogKEICAgICTz__2LQ%7C%7C?hl=en"],["https://www.google.com/local/content/rap/report?postId=ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNUel9fMkxREAE&t=1&entityid=ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNUel9fMkxREi4KF0NJSE0wb2dLRUlDQWdJQ1R6X18yclFFEhNDZ3dJdmJ5dHNnWVFzTEhTa2dFGi0KFkNJSE0wb2dLRUlDQWdJQ1R6X18yYlESE0Nnd0l2Ynl0c2dZUXNMSFNrZ0UiEgkAAAAAAAAAABFg0CkD60WozioTQ2d3SXZieXRzZ1lRc0xIU2tnRQ&wv=1&d=286732320",null,null,"0ahUKEwi3xKvwuquTAxWzA2MBHagVNsgQoykIEygB"],null,[null,[[1,3]]]],"0ahUKEwi3xKvwuquTAxWzA2MBHagVNsgQ0pMFCBEoBQ"],null,"CAESY0NBRVFHaHBFUTJwRlNVRlNTWEJEWjI5QlVEY3lTRUp3YkMxRFJWOWZSV2hDWkhOT1JGOU9PV2RGTWxkek4ycHhRVUZCUVVGQlIyZHVPVEkxT0VOalIyMVlORWxSV1VGRFNVRQ=="],[["ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNqdTdMbnlBRRAB",["0x0:0xcea845eb0329d060",null,1714115544789772,1714115544789772,[null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/103886828405562393341/reviews?hl=en"],null,null,["Saada","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocIhQe26ii5b6Tf7ig3Y8ESEqtHAqeHdXiO8WSWiIL5PD6Dnew=s120-c-rp-mo-br100",["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/103886828405562393341?hl=en"],"103886828405562393341",null,1,0,null,[0,1,1],0,["1
